english_translation: While you are reading this book, pay close attention to the words used by the author, because they have depth and offer valuable lessons that apply to our everyday lives.

dialogue.shona: Paunenge uchiverenga bhuku iri, nyatsoteerera mazwi akashandiswa nemunyori; nokuti ane udzamu, uye anopa dzidziso yakakosha inoshanda muupenyu hwedu hwemazuva ose.
dialogue.english: While you are reading this book, pay close attention to the words used by the author, because they have depth and offer valuable lessons that apply to our everyday lives.
dialogue.literal_gloss: Paunenge [on / at unenge] • uchiverenga [uchiverenga] • bhuku [book] • iri [iri] • nyatsoteerera [nyatsoteerera] • mazwi [plural zwi] • akashandiswa [he/she (past) shandiswa] • nemunyori [and / with munyori] • nokuti [because] • ane [ane] • udzamu [udzamu] • uye [and / furthermore] • anopa [he/she pa] • dzidziso [dzidziso] • yakakosha [it (past) kosha] • inoshanda [it shanda] • muupenyu [in / singular upenyu] • hwedu [hwedu]

grammar_notes.title: Talking About the Past ('akashandiswa')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'akashandiswa' expresses a completed past action. Shona has two main ways to talk about the past: 1) For actions that happened earlier today or very recently, combine the short subject prefix ('nda-' = I, 'wa-' = you, 'a-' = he/she, 'ta-' = we, 'va-' = they) directly with the verb stem (e.g., 'ndamuka' = 'I woke up today', 'wabudirira' = 'you have succeeded'). 2) For events that happened yesterday or further in the past, insert '-ka-' after the subject prefix (e.g., 'takatenga' = 'we bought', 'vakaenda' = 'they went', 'akadanidzira' = 'he shouted').
grammar_notes.rule: Recent Today Past: [nda- / wa- / ta- / va-] + verb | Earlier Past: [ndaka- / waka- / taka- / vaka-] + verb

grammar_notes.title: Present Tense & Everyday Actions ('anopa')
grammar_notes.content: The verb 'anopa' uses the present marker '-no-'. In Shona, inserting '-no-' between the subject prefix and the verb stem expresses general truths, everyday habits, or states of mind like 'wanting', 'thinking', and 'knowing'. For example: 'ndinoda' ('I want/like'), 'unofunga' ('you think'), 'vanoti' ('they say'), and 'vanorima' ('they farm').
grammar_notes.rule: [ndi- (I) / u- (you) / a- (he/she) / ti- (we) / va- (they)] + -no- + verb -> Ndinoda (I want), Vanogara (They live)

grammar_notes.title: Possessive Pronouns: Saying 'My', 'Your', and 'Our' ('muupenyu')
grammar_notes.content: In Shona, possessive words like 'muupenyu' ('my/your/our/their') always follow the noun they belong to! The six core possessive stems are '-ngu' (my), '-ko' (your), '-ke' (his/her/its), '-du' (our), '-nyu' (your plural/polite), and '-vo' (their). A short linking sound ('wa-', 'ya-', 'ra-', 'cha-', 'dza-', 'ma-') attaches to the front of the stem to match the noun: for example, 'shamwari yangu' (my friend), 'munda wako' (your field), 'mabhuku edu' (our books), and 'kubudirira kwenyu' (your success).

cultural_notes.title: Appreciating Literary Depth ('Udzamu') & Moral Lessons ('Dzidziso') in Shona Books
cultural_notes.content: Shona literature prizes 'udzamu' (linguistic depth and richness of expression) and 'dzidziso yakakosha' (practical moral wisdom that enriches everyday life).

active_exercises.prompt: How do you say 'There is a cup of water on the table' in Shona?
active_exercises.explanation: 'Patafura' ('on the table') pairs with 'pane' ('there is at/on that spot') + 'kapu yemvura' ('a cup of water').

active_exercises.prompt: Translate this new sentence into English: 'Ndasiya nharembozha yangu pachigaro mumba yokutandarira.'
options: Please close the door and all the windows before sleeping.
My keys are inside the small bag on the table.
We are sitting under the shade tree outside the house.
I left my mobile phone on the chair in the living room.
active_exercises.correct_answer: I left my mobile phone on the chair in the living room.
active_exercises.explanation: 'Ndasiya' = 'I left', 'nharembozha yangu' = 'my mobile phone', 'pachigaro' = 'on the chair', 'mumba yokutandarira' = 'in the living room'.

active_exercises.prompt: In 'Shiri diki dziri kuimba pamusoro pemuti', what are the small birds doing?
options: Singing at the top of the tree
Looking for seeds in the field
active_exercises.correct_answer: Singing at the top of the tree
active_exercises.explanation: 'Shiri diki' = 'small birds', 'dziri kuimba' = 'are singing', 'pamusoro pemuti' = 'at the top of the tree'.
